hardGateFindings.finding: External reader, collaborator, application, and hiring outcomes remain not-yet-measured. Reader and field actions are explicitly planned, their receipts are not returned, and repository or LLM activity cannot advance those states.

All eight blind spots have named signals, controls, triggers, owners, decision rules, next tests, and evidence-return paths. Live inquiry, source-balance, composition, role-evidence, mosaic, and field-action artifacts make each risk capable of changing state.

The protocol and checker distinguish deterministic checks, separate read-only LLM judge sessions, orchestration receipts, and external human validation. They require common-digest binding, distinct sessions, generator exclusion, artifact hashes, and disclosure that repository provenance is auditable process evidence rather than cryptographic proof.

Record-level public-safety checks are supplemented by a current combination-level mosaic review covering affiliations, movement, collaborator patterns, protected records, social traces, and feedback. The controls prohibit private feedback, identifying receipts, participant-level joins, and raw relationship graphs while retaining explicit unresolved risks.

requiredRevisions: Change the KC Town Hall work-card, metadata, Known block, and case-study stewardship-transition language to explicit first-person attribution such as “Jamie reports,” matching the mixed evidence basis instead of presenting the transition as independently established.

Extend the render-derived control so every authored individual-role proposition is bound to a canonical claim or proof ID and evidence basis. Fail public prose that bypasses the first-person or mixed attribution rule even when the corresponding Knowledge Bank projection and proof wording are correctly bounded.
limitations: This is an LLM repository-control evaluation, not human reader research, collaborator review, deployment approval, application evidence, or a hiring outcome. External outcomes remain not-yet-measured.

The reader study, hiring-reader solicitation, and job-search follow-through are planned and have no returned receipts; this judgment evaluates their specificity and enforceability, not completion or effectiveness.
Prior judge artifacts, prior result scores, and the stale current run were excluded, so no comparative regression determination was made.
Repository provenance and orchestration controls provide auditable process evidence, not cryptographic proof of independence, factual truth, or external usefulness.
